agree

throw away
To get rid of something that you no longer need or want.
Do not throw away plastic containers that can be recycled easily.
give back
To return something to the person who owns or lent it.
Remember to give back the borrowed library books on time tomorrow.
come across
To find or meet someone or something by chance without searching.
I happened to come across an old photograph inside an old book.
blow up
To fill with air or cause something to explode with force.
We helped to blow up fifty colourful balloons for the party.
hold on
To wait for a short time, especially on the telephone line.
Please hold on for a moment while I transfer your call.
go on
To continue happening or taking place without stopping or changing direction.
The noise in the street will go on until late night.
call back
To return a telephone call to someone who phoned you earlier.
I will call back as soon as I finish my dinner.
write down
To record information on paper using a pen or pencil instrument.
Be sure to write down the assignment details in your notebook.
bring up
To raise a child or mention a topic in a conversation.
Parents work hard to bring up their children with good values.
cut down on
To reduce the amount or quantity of something you consume daily.
You should cut down on sugary drinks to improve your health.
get over
To recover from an illness, disappointment, or difficult emotional experience.
It took him several months to get over the lost match.
look into
To investigate or examine the facts about a situation or problem.
The police promised to look into the reported noise complaint tonight.
run into
To meet someone unexpectedly or collide with an object while moving.
I was surprised to run into my former primary teacher today.
stand out
To be easily noticed because of being different, extraordinary, or distinctive.
Her bright red coat made her stand out in crowd.
turn on
To start the operation of a machine or device using switch.
Please turn on the light because it is getting dark inside.
turn off
To stop the operation of a machine, light, or appliance.
Remember to turn off the computer when you finish working today.
show up
To arrive at a place, especially when expected or invited.
Only half of the invited guests chose to show up on time.
put on
To place a garment or clothing item onto your physical body.
Be sure to put on a warm coat before going outside.
log in
To enter security credentials to gain access to a computer system.
You need to log in with your password to view emails.
sign up
To register your name formally to join an activity or organization.
Many students decided to sign up for the drama club this term.
carry out
To perform or conduct a task, test, or research experiment.
Scientists plan to carry out more tests before publishing their results.
figure out
To understand or solve a problem after thinking about it deeply.
It took me a long time to figure out how to operate.
speed up
To move faster or cause something to happen at greater rate.
Drivers need to speed up when entering the main motorway lane.
slow down
To reduce your speed or cause something to move more slowly.
You must slow down when driving near a primary school zone.
take over
To assume control or responsibility for something previously managed by another.
A new manager will take over the department starting next month.
break out
To start suddenly, referring to war, fire, or severe disease.
A violent storm threatens to break out across the coastal area.
end up
To reach a particular place, state, or situation after actions.
If you do not plan, you might end up lost in city.
keep away
To avoid going near someone or something to stay safe.
Warning signs tell visitors to keep away from dangerous deep water.
